 Judgment

The Police Inspector of HSR Layout Traffic Police Station has filed charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC & Sec.146 R/w Sec.196 of MV Act.
2.

The brief facts of the prosecution case are as under: -
That on 22.03.2024 at 10.30 a.m. accused being the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-09- AQ-3895 drove the same within the jurisdiction of HSR Traffic Police station on 27 th Main road from Vemana Circle towards Ring road at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and near Embassy Elegant Building hit to pedestrian C.W.2 when he was crossing the road from Embassy Elegant building CC No.3376/2024 towards CPW Quarters, as a result C.W.1 fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his right hand and left leg and accused also sustained grievous injuries.
Further, at the time of accident offending vehicle did not have valid insurance.
As such the accused has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC & Sec.134(A & B) R/w Sec.187 of MV Act.
3. Cognizance was taken by perusing the prosecution papers and materials, the accused on receipt of summons appeared before the court and got himself enlarged on bail.

On the said date the prosecution papers were furnished to the accused as per Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. and substance of accusation in the form of plea was read over and explained to him, accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
4. During the course of trial the prosecution has examined PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 10.
The statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded the accused had no explanation and he denied the incriminating circumstances appearing against him.
The counsel for the accused filed written argument and heard argument on prosecution side and perused the materials available on record.

6. The point that arises for my determination is as under:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 22.03.2024 at 10.30 a.m. accused being the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-09-AQ-3895 drove the same within the jurisdiction of HSR Traffic Police station on 27th Main road from Vemana Circle towards Ring road at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC?

thereby accused committed an offence punishable U/Sec.338 of IPC ?

9. The prosecution case against the accused is that on 22.03.2024 at 10.30 a.m. accused being the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-09-AQ-3895 drove the same within the jurisdiction of HSR Traffic Police station on 27th Main road from Vemana Circle towards Ring road at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and near Embassy Elegant Building hit to pedestrian C.W.2 when CC No.3376/2024 he was crossing the road from Embassy Elegant building towards CPW Quarters, as a result C.W.1 fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his right hand and left leg and accused also sustained grievous injuries.
Further, at the time of accident offending vehicle did not have valid insurance.
10. In order to bring home the charge against the accused the prosecution has examined 5 witnesses as PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 10.

Ex.P.1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar,
Ex.P.3 is the rough sketch, Ex.P.4 is the FIR, Ex.P.5 & 6 are the notice and reply U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.7 is the IMV report, Ex.P.8 & 9 are the wound certificate and Ex.P.10 is the 2 photos.
11. Before adverting to the appreciation of evidence it is proper to state in brief the evidence deposed by the prosecution witnesses.

sentences.text: C.W.1 examined as P.W.1 is the complainant of this case.

She deposed that, she is working at HSR layout CPW Complex and her father is working as security guard at Dominos Pizza and on 22.03.2024 at 9.15 to 9.30 a.m. when her father was crossing the road on white line of the road to go to Dominoz pizza one two wheeler bearing No.KL-09-AQ-3895 came in high speed and hit to her father, as a result her father sustained grievous injuries on his head and right leg and rider of the two wheeler also sustained injuries.
Further her father was taken for treatment at Lotus hospital and Hosmat hospital.
On the accident day at 5.30 p.m. she lodged a complaint as per Ex.P.1.
Further she deposed that, she has signed on Ex.P.2/spot mahazar at police station one month after the accident.
Further she deposed that, accident has occurred due to the fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In her cross examination she has admitted that she turned towards the spot of accident only after she heard the sound from the accident and hence she does not know the manner in which accused was driving his vehicle.
She has admitted CC No.3376/2024 that, there was no signal in the spot of accident and there was no provision for pedestrians to cross the road.
13. C.W.2 examined as P.W.2 is the victim of this case.
He deposed that, he is working as security guard in one building situated at 27 th cross.

On 22.03.2024 at 9.30 a.m. he was crossing the road on the median at HSR Lay out 27th Main, 15th cross by observing the vehicles coming on the road at that time one vehicle came and hit to him and his daughter shifted him to hospital and 2 days after the accident he came into consciousness and police obtained his statement.
In his cross examination he has admitted that, there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the road in the spot of accident.
He has admitted that he does not know the speed of the offending the vehicle, registration number of the offending vehicle, make of the offending vehicle.
He has admitted that, he has not observed the offending vehicle coming towards him before the accident.
CC No.3376/2024 14. C.W.5 examined as P.W.3 is the mahazar witness of this case.

He deposed that, he and C.W.6 signed on Ex.P.2 on 22.03.2024 at 10.00 a.m. at HSR Layout, 27th Main road, opposite to CPW Quarters, in front of Elegant Embassy building and on that day he also signed on Ex.P.3.
In his cross examination he has stated that he went for mahazar voluntarily.
He has admitted that he signed Ex.P.2 in police station.
He has admitted that, victim in this case is his uncle.
15. C.W.12 examined as P.W.4 is the Investigating Officer.
He has deposed as per the investigation conducted by him.
In the cross examination he has stated that C.W.1 has mentioned the registration number of the offending vehicle in the complaint.
16. C.W.13 examined as P.W5 is another investigating officer and he has deposed about the investigation conducted by him.

In the cross examination he has admitted that accused could not observe the pedestrian because of heavy traffic and there was no CC No.3376/2024 provision for the pedestrian to cross the road in spot of accident.
He has admitted that, even the accused has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

He has further admitted that the accident occurred because the pedestrian came in the way of the accused vehicle all of a sudden forcing the accused to Hsr Layout Tr Ps vs Irafan Rider Of Mc No Kl09Aq3895 on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20204204/
4 apply sudden break of his vehicle and as a result accused vehicle collided with the pedestrian and even the accused fell down and sustained injuries.

sentences.text: He has admitted that he has not taken photographs at the time of the mahazar.
17. With the above evidence, this court has to ascertain whether the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.

In order to prove offence U/Sec.279 of IPC the prosecution has to prove;
(i) Rash and negligent driving on public way (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

To prove an offence U/sec.338 of IPC the prosecution has to prove that some grievous hurt was caused to a person, that such hurt was caused by rash or negligent act of the accused and the act was such that it caused endangerment to human life or public safety of others.
19.
After marshalling all the oral and documentary evidence it is crystal clear that, there is no dispute about the accused driving the offending vehicle on the date of the accident.
There is no dispute about the P.W.2 having sustained injuries in the said accident.
There is no dispute regarding IMV report as per Ex.P.7, which states that there is no mechanical defects in the offending vehicle.
Since, the injuries sustained by P.W.2 is not disputed and it is not denied that the accused was driving the offending vehicle.
The Court only needs to consider if there was any negligence or rashness on the part of the accused due to which the accident occurred.
20. In this regard the prosecution has examined P.W.1 who is the eye witness and P.W.2 who is the victim CC No.3376/2024 witness.
P.W.1 is the daughter of P.W.2.
Admittedly both are interested witnesses since they stand to gain in terms of compensation.
Hence, their evidence can be accepted only if it is corroborated with other evidence on record.

Even though P.W.1 is an eye witness in her cross examination she has clearly admitted that she turned towards the spot of accident only after she heard the sound from the accident and hence she has not observed the manner in which accused was driving his vehicle.
She has stated that, since her father was thrown at a distance she is deposing that the accused was driving the vehicle at a high speed.
Here it is pertinent to note that neither P.W.1 nor P.W.2 have deposed anything about P.W.2 being flung to a distance at the time of accident in their examination in chief.
Therefore it is clearly an improvement made by her at the time of the cross examination to justify that accused has driven negligently.
She has further admitted that there was no provision for pedestrians to cross the road in the spot of accident.
She has also admitted that, she and C.W.6 signed Ex.P.2 in the police station and she has not visited the spot of accident along with the police.
Therefore from her evidence prosecution is unable to prove rashness or negligence of the accused.

sentences.text: P.W.2 is the victim witness and in his cross examination he has stated that, when he was standing on the median accused came in his vehicle and hit him.
But Ex.P.2 and 3 do not mention anything about a median.
In Ex.P.3 there are 2 lines drawn and the accident spot is shown next to the lines but there is no mention in Ex.P.2 or 3 that the said 2 lines are the median.
Even P.W.5 who is the IO does not speak anything about a median.
Further he has admitted that, he has not seen the offending vehicle before the accident and therefore he does not know the manner in which accused was driving his vehicle.
Therefore even from evidence of P.W.2 prosecution is unable to prove rashness or negligence of the accused.

Further, P.W.5 who is the IO in his cross examination has categorically admitted that the accident occurred because the pedestrian came in the way of the accused vehicle all of a sudden because of which accused had to apply the breaks of his vehicle leading to a collision between the CC No.3376/2024 accused and pedestrian and as a result both the accused and pedestrian have sustained injuries.
From the evidence of P.W.5 it is clear that there is no rashness or negligence on part of the accused.
Rather contributory negligence on behalf of P.W.2 cannot be ruled out.
22. Here it is pertinent to consider Ex.P.2/spot mahazar and Ex.P.3/rough sketch.
The said rough sketch and spot mahazar is prepared in presence of P.W.1, 3 and 6 as per IO.
As per the mahazar P.W.1 has identified the spot of accident.

But P.W.1 in her examination in chief and cross examination has stated that she never visited the spot of accident along with police and she signed to the mahazar in the police station along with C.W.6.
Whereas P.W.3 who is a mahazar witness has deposed in complete contradiction to P.W.1 and stated that, he has visited the spot of accident.
Even P.W.3 has admitted that, he signed to Ex.P. 2 in the police station.
Therefore, considering evidence of P.W.1 and 3 it is evident that Ex.P.2 and 3 have been prepared by the police as per their requirement.
Even the I.O., in his cross examination has admitted that, there was CC No.3376/2024 negligence by the victim in crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing.
Moreover, even if evidence of P.W.1 and 2 is taken at face value both the witnesses have vaguely stated that accused came at a high speed without mentioning the speed.
23. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Karnataka V/s Sathish reported in 1998 SCC (Cri) 1508 has stated that, driving at a high speed by itself does not imply negligence or rashness.

entities.text: State of Karnataka V/s Sathish reported in 1998 SCC (Cri) 1508
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Negligence or rashness would have to be established as a fact.
In this case there is only a bare statement made by P.W.1 and 2 that the offending vehicle was driven at a high speed.
No attempt has been made to establish that there was rashness on the part of the accused.
The expression high speed could range from 30 k.m. per hour to 100 k.m. per hour.
The speed limit in the particular road is also not on record.
Therefore, prosecution is unable to prove rashness or negligence of the accused.
24. It is the burden of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused.
The evidence placed on record CC No.3376/2024 do not rise up to the expectation to prove beyond reasonable doubt in so far as the involvement of accused in the incident is concerned.
Therefore, the prosecution version that on the account of rash and negligent driving by the accused, accident has occurred cannot be held to be proved.

25. By ascertaining all these oral and documentary evidence it is clear that, there is no substantive,
cogent and corroborative evidence to prove the guilt of the accused.

Hence, mere evidence of official Hsr Layout Tr Ps vs Irafan Rider Of Mc No Kl09Aq3895 on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20204204/
6 witnesses is insufficient to prove the guilt of accused.

Therefore, by considering the overall facts and circumstances of this case, this court is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, point Nos.1 & 2 are answered in the Negative.
26.
The prosecution has also alleged that, the accused did not possess valid insurance at the time of the accident.
U/sec.106 of Indian evidence act the CC No.3376/2024 burden of proof is on the accused to produce valid driving insurance.
However accused has not submitted any document in this regard.
As already discussed prosecution is able to prove that accused was driving vehicle No.KL-09-AQ-3895 at the time of the accident.
Hence, accused has complete offences punishable U/sec.146 r/w sec.196 of IMV Act.
Hence, point No.3 is answered in the affirmative.
27. Point No.4:

In view of the findings on point Nos.1 to 3, this court proceeds to pass the following;
 ORDER  Acting under Sec.255(1) of Cr.P.C. accused is hereby acquitted for accusation of commission of the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

Acting U/s.255(2) of Criminal  Procedure code, the accused is  hereby convicted of the offences  CC No.3376/2024  punishable U/Sec.146 R/w Sec.196  of MV Act.
 Accused is sentenced to pay  fine of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees one  thousand only) for the offence  punishable U/Sec.146 R/w Sec.196  of MV Act.
In default he shall  undergo simple imprisonment for a  period one month.

His bail bond and surety  bond stands cancelled after the  lapse of appeal period.
